title: Oxidation of Alcohols
author: 3iGR44tcGMnRnhEYm
chapter_outcomes: Recall the reactions (reagents and conditions) by which alcohols can be produced; (a) electrophilic addition of steam to an alkene, $\mathrm{H_2 O_{(g)}}$ and $\mathrm{H_3 PO_4}$ catalyst; (b) reaction of alkenes with cold dilute acidified potassium manganate($\mathbf{VII}$) to form a diol; (c) substitution of a halogenoalkane using $\mathrm{NaOH(aq)}$ and heat; (d) reduction of an aldehyde or ketone using $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ or $\mathrm{LiA}l \mathrm{H_4}$; (e) reduction of a carboxylic acid using $\mathrm{LiA}l \mathrm{H_4}$; (f) hydrolysis of an ester using dilute acid or dilute alkali and heat

Describe the reaction with oxygen (combustion), substitution to form halogenoalkanes, e.g. by reaction with HX(g) or with $\mathrm{KCl}$ and concentrated $\mathrm{H_2 SO_4}$ or concentrated $\mathrm{H_3 PO_4}$ or with $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ and heat or with $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ or with $\mathrm{SOCl}_2$, the reaction with $\mathrm{Na(s)}$, oxidation with acidified $\mathrm{K_2 Cr_2 O_7}$ or acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ to carbonyl compounds by distillation and carboxylic acids by refluxing (primary alcohols give aldehydes which can be further oxidised to carboxylic acids, secondary alcohols give ketones, tertiary alcohols cannot be oxidised), dehydration to an alkene, by using a heated catalyst, e.g. $\mathrm{Al_2 O_3}$ or a concentrated acid, and formation of esters by reaction with carboxylic acids and concentrated H2 SO4 as catalyst as exemplified by ethanol
Classify alcohols as primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols, to include examples with more than one alcohol group
State characteristic distinguishing reactions, e.g. mild oxidation with acidified $\mathrm{K_2 Cr_2 O_7}$, colour change from orange to green

Deduce the presence of a $\mathrm{CH_3 CH(OH)–}$ group in an alcohol, $\mathrm{CH_3 CH(OH)–R}$, from its reaction with alkaline $\mathrm{I_2(aq)}$ to form a yellow precipitate of tri-iodomethane and an ion, $\mathrm{RCO_2^-}$
Explain the acidity of alcohols compared with water
